If you only read one page, read this one. The [coverage board](/coverage.qmd) is the longer gauge list.

## What happened in the data

The Pacific’s published seasonal temperature index (ONI, May–July) is **warm (+1.39)**. That is one ocean product, not a weather forecast for your town.

Satellites counted about **5,000** fire hotspots in a day. One large part of the map returned **zero** while another part returned thousands. Zero there is a **blind spot**, not a safe zone.

The rain dataset we use for history is still sitting on **July**. August rain from that source is not in yet. Missing is not drought.

The Atlantic current people argue about (AMOC) is **not updated here**. We will not pretend it is.

## What that does *not* mean

It does not mean the world is ending this week.  
It does not mean you should leave your country.  
It does not mean last year’s rain will repeat, or fail, at your house.  
It does not decide the parked claims about volcanic winter or “move to the Goldilocks band.”

A separate check of 29 winters found that when that Pacific index was high, **Ubay and Manaus rain tended to run the other way**, **Nairobi the same way**, and **Mumbai and Paris looked like chance**. Same ocean, different places. That is a history test, not next season’s forecast.

## If you want something useful to do

- Read the warning page of **your** weather and fire agency before this site.
- Keep ordinary reserves people already know: water, a week of medicine, papers, a neighbor who will check on you.
- If officials say evacuate or boil water, do that. This brief does not override them.
- If officials have not said that, do not invent an evacuation from a hotspot count.

## If you are thinking about land, tanks, or “off-grid”

Wait until there is a **named river basin** with a water and hazard sheet. Nine dots on a map are not that sheet.
